title: The Poem Exalts Mani Singh Above Earlier Martyrs

blocks.text: After describing the final cuts, the narrative turns from the scene of execution to praise. It compares Bhai Mani Singh with famous sufferers such as Mansur, yet insists that Mani Singh bore a still harsher trial because his body was severed joint by joint before death.

The page argues that he remained greater than Mansur because he kept Sikhi intact under torture and refused every inducement to break faith. His martyrdom is treated not as a private death but as the fulfillment of the congregation’s prophecy and the triumph of disciplined devotion.

The poet closes by ranking him among the foremost Sikh martyrs and by fixing the event in remembered history. The tone becomes commemorative, preparing the transition from the execution itself to the wider aftermath of Mani Singh’s death.
